title: 2/4 and 3/4 time
summary: March in 2 and waltz in 3, and hear where the strong beat falls.

hook.text: Soldiers march: left, right, left, right. Dancers waltz, as in *The Blue Danube*: ONE, two, three, ONE, two, three. Press play and tap your foot to this tune. Which of the two does it feel like?

explore.text: Your turn. This music has only 3 beats in every [[bar|bar]]. Count out loud: ONE, two, three, and tap the pad on every note. Lean harder on every ONE. After three, start again. Do not count to four.
explore.goal: Tap all 4 [[bar|bars]] while you count 1, 2, 3 in every one.

cards.text: The top number of 3/4 is 3, so every [[bar|bar]] holds 3 beats and you count 1, 2, 3. That is [[triple-time|triple time]]: the first beat is strong and the other two are weak. It is the waltz feel.
2/4 has 2 beats in each [[bar|bar]], so you count 1, 2. That is [[duple-time|duple time]]: beat 1 is strong and beat 2 is weak. It is the march feel.

The bottom number is still 4, so each beat is still a [[crotchet|crotchet]]. A 3/4 [[bar|bar]] holds 3 [[crotchet|crotchets]], or a [[minim|minim]] and a [[crotchet|crotchet]]. A 2/4 [[bar|bar]] holds 2 [[crotchet|crotchets]] or one [[minim|minim]]. A [[semibreve|semibreve]] is too long for either.

alternative.text: Try it with your body. March on the spot: LEFT, right, LEFT, right. That is 2 steps, then round again. Now waltz: STEP, sway, sway. Count the sway-sway and you find 3. The big move is always beat 1.

questions.prompt: What does the time signature tell you?
questions.hint: The top number counts beats in each [[bar|bar]]. The bottom 4 means each beat is a [[crotchet|crotchet]].

questions.prompt: Both clips tick at the same speed. One groups its beats in 3s, like a waltz. Which one?
questions.hint: Listen for the high note: it marks beat 1. How many ticks fit between one high note and the next?

options.reason: Clip A has a high note every 2 ticks: high, low, high, low. That is a march in 2/4. The waltz in clip B has a high note every 3 ticks.

questions.prompt: Every [[bar|bar]] here should hold 3 beats. One has too many. Tap it.
questions.hint: In 3/4 every [[bar|bar]] comes to 3, not 4. Count each one.

payload.explanation: [[bar|Bar]] 2 has 4 beats: a [[crotchet|crotchet]] (1), a [[minim|minim]] (2) and another [[crotchet|crotchet]] (1). In 3/4 every [[bar|bar]] holds 3 beats, so it has one too many.

questions.prompt: In 3/4, which beat is the strong one?
questions.hint: Think of the waltz: ONE, two, three. Which number gets the big step?

options.reason: Beat 3 is a weak beat. In 3/4 the strong beat comes first, on beat 1, followed by two weak beats.
The beats are not equal. Beat 1 is strong and beats 2 and 3 are weak: that is what makes a waltz sway.

questions.hint: Count 1, 2, 3 and start again each time you reach 3 beats. A [[minim|minim]] counts as 2.

points: 3/4 has 3 beats in each [[bar|bar]]. It is [[triple-time|triple time]], the waltz feel: beat 1 is strong, beats 2 and 3 are weak.
2/4 has 2 beats in each [[bar|bar]]. It is [[duple-time|duple time]], the march feel: beat 1 is strong, beat 2 is weak.
The bottom 4 still means each beat is a [[crotchet|crotchet]], so count the [[bar|bar]] in [[crotchet|crotchets]]: 3 in 3/4, 2 in 2/4.
